label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Hi D. Bergeron and everyone,

You’re right to ask for a straight answer, especially if you have a carnet with bread still on it. I’m sorry the sign made people worry.

**We are not closing for good or moving. I bought the building!** I wanted to keep it a surprise for the reopening, but I can see that wasn’t such a good idea.

And to answer your question clearly: **all the carnets are still good, with no expiry date.** If you have seven loaves left, you still have seven loaves waiting for you. We sold 214 carnets in October, at $60 for 12 loaves, and every one of them will be honoured. In January, each carnet holder can also have a free croissant, with my thanks.

If you would rather have your money back for your carnet, please come see me at the bakery and I will give it back, no questions asked.

The bakery will be closed **January 4 to 18 for work**, and we’ll reopen **Tuesday, January 19 at 7 a.m.** Then on **Saturday, January 23**, I would love to invite everyone to celebrate with us. Come by for a coffee and a free piece of the new bread. You don’t need to have a carnet, just come say hello!

Marc-Antoine, your cousin was half right: the building was sold. It was sold to me! M. Ferland, our landlord, is 81 and retiring to Sherbrooke to be with his daughter. He offered to sell it to me before anyone else, and we signed at the notary on December 15.

I also want to reassure everyone asking about the apartments upstairs: **the three apartments will stay rented, with the same tenants and the same rent.** I promised the tenants that in writing.

M. Ferland has come in every morning for 17 years for his baguette *pas trop cuite*. He cried a little at the notary, and I think that tells you how much this place means to him too. I’m very grateful he gave me the chance to buy it.

During the two weeks we’re closed, we’re getting a new four-deck oven from a supplier in Laval. Our old oven is from 1998 and broke three times this year, so I think it has earned its retirement! We’re also taking over the space at the back, which used to be storage for the dépanneur. We’ll have six small tables there, so finally you’ll be able to sit down.

And about that sign: my nephew Thomas wrote it at six in the morning. “Grande nouvelle” was his idea, and I said OK without thinking about how it would look. The half-empty shelves on the 28th weren’t a sign of closing either. We sold everything for Christmas Eve, including 400 bûches!

I understand why people were worried. Mile End has lost many small shops, and nobody wants to see another one go. Still, seeing the word “scam” hurt after 17 years on this street. I hope you know now that nobody is losing their bread or their money.

Thank you, Priya, for your kind words, and thank you to everyone who spoke up for us and everyone who has supported Le Pétrin Doré since we opened on the Fairmount corner in March 2009. You’ve made it possible for me to take this next step.

I hope to see you on January 23. I’m very happy I can finally share the news with you.

Hélène  
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré
